purpose: Tedizolid is an antibiotic used to treat a type of serious skin infection called acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSIs). These infections are often caused by bacteria like MRSA, which can be hard to treat with common antibiotics. Your doctor may prescribe it as a pill or as an IV infusion given in a hospital or clinic.
how_it_works: Tedizolid works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and survive. Think of it like pulling the plug on the bacteria's ability to reproduce. Without being able to make these important proteins, the bacteria die off and your infection clears up.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, headache, diarrhea, vomiting, and dizziness. Some people may also notice a decrease in certain blood cells, which your doctor may monitor with blood tests. Most side effects are mild, but let your doctor or pharmacist know if anything bothers you.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are taking certain antidepressants called MAOIs or serotonin-related medicines, as combining them with tedizolid can cause a dangerous reaction called serotonin syndrome. This medicine may lower your white blood cell count, so tell your doctor if you get a fever or feel unusually tired. If you have a history of low blood counts or are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medication. Finish your full course of treatment even if you feel better, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 200 mg once a day for 6 days. It can be taken as a tablet by mouth, with or without food, or given as an IV infusion over one hour in a medical setting. Try to take it at the same time each day and do not skip doses.
